Case 1: 45-Year-Old Male with Chest Pain: A 45-year-old male presents to the ED with sudden onset severe chest pain radiating to the back. BP is 160/90 in the right arm and 120/70 in the left arm.

What is the most likely diagnosis?

A) Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS)
B) Pulmonary Embolism
C) Aortic Dissection
D) Pericarditis

[b]Correct Answer: C) Aortic Dissection[/b]

[b]Why C is correct:[/b]
The patient presents with tearing chest pain radiating to the back, and a significant blood pressure difference between arms.

[b]Why the other options are incorrect:[/b]

[b]A) Acute Coronary Syndrome:[/b] Usually presents with crushing chest pain, but the ECG is normal here.

[b]B) Pulmonary Embolism:[/b] Typically presents with sudden dyspnea and pleuritic chest pain.
